meta.description: Divalent lanthanides and 4f-5d levels: free-ion references (NIST), host data with sources, Dorenbos empirical relations. Energies in cm-1 unless stated; nm are vacuum-equivalent 1e7/E unless the source quotes air wavelengths.
meta.caveat: Host values were extracted from open web pages with an automated reader; each carries 'verify' where the primary number was not seen verbatim in a table.

Ce3+ (Ce IV).source: NIST Atomic Spectra Database (Kramida, Ralchenko, Reader & NIST ASD Team), physics.nist.gov/asd, levels retrieved 2026-09-29 via WebFetch (automated text extraction — spot-check against the live table before publication)
Ce3+ (Ce IV).note: Free-ion lowest 4f->5d = 49,737 cm-1 (6.17 eV). Dorenbos papers use E_free(Ce3+) = 6.12 eV (49,340 cm-1) as reference for the redshift D — recalled standard value, verify (Dorenbos, J. Lumin. 91, 91 (2000)). A secondary source quotes "the cerium 5d levels of the free ion, at 6.35 eV" (Sr2SiS4 paper, Materials 6, 3663 (2013)) — that number appears to be a centroid-type value.

Eu2+ (Eu III).source: NIST Atomic Spectra Database (Kramida, Ralchenko, Reader & NIST ASD Team), physics.nist.gov/asd, levels retrieved 2026-09-29 via WebFetch (automated text extraction — spot-check against the live table before publication)
Eu2+ (Eu III).note: Dorenbos uses 34,000 cm-1 (4.215 eV) for the free-ion first f-d transition; quoted as "34004 cm-1 for the free Eu2+ ion" in arXiv:1709.00311 (Jia et al., citing Dorenbos J. Lumin. 104, 239 (2003)).

dorenbos_relations.redshift_definition: D(n+,A) = E_free(Ln, first f->d) - E(Ln, A) (host-induced lowering of first 4f->5d absorption); for a given host A, D is nearly the same for all Ln of the same charge (Dorenbos).
dorenbos_relations.E_Eu2_vs_E_Ce3: E(Eu2+,A) = 0.64 E(Ce3+,A) + 0.53 eV (first f-d transition energies)
dorenbos_relations.source: Relations quoted in Materials 6, 3663 (2013) [Sr2SiS4 Ce/Eu paper, eqs. 1,3,4] and arXiv:1709.00311 eq. 36, both citing P. Dorenbos, J. Lumin. 104, 239 (2003) "Energy of the first 4f7->4f65d transition of Eu2+ in inorganic compounds" (and Dorenbos J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 15, 575 (2003) for the Ce3+/Eu2+ relation — verify which paper each equation originates from).
dorenbos_relations.consistency_check: With E_free(Eu2+)=4.215 eV and E_free(Ce3+)=6.12 eV the two forms are equivalent: 4.215 - (0.64*(6.12-E_Ce) - 0.233) = 0.64 E_Ce + 0.53 eV (checked: 4.215+0.233-0.64*6.12 = 0.531).

hosts.source: "Optically pumped Ce:LaF3 laser at 286 nm", Opt. Lett. 5, 339 (1980) (Ehrlich, Moulton, Osgood) — abstract: tuning ~275–315 nm

User-supplied estimate (~40,000 cm-1 = 250 nm); consistent with 250 nm Ce3+ excitation used in Frontiers in Chemistry 13, 1501039 (2025) (LaF3:Ce/Gd/Eu) and the 245 nm Ce3+ absorption noted in Radzhabov & Shendrik arXiv:1511.00385. Exact band maximum from Dorenbos J. Lumin. 91, 91 (2000) (fluorides) NOT verified in this session.
Materials 14, 4243 (2021) "Energy Structure and Luminescence of CeF3 Crystals" (dips in CeF3 spectra correlated with 5d1..5d5 maxima); emission 282/305 nm (regular Ce3+) and 290/340 nm bands
Chin. Opt. Lett. 14, 061601 (2016) "Ce3+ ion-doped alpha-NaYF4 single crystal for UV laser" (abstract)
arXiv:1709.00311 (Jia et al., first-principles study of Eu2+ phosphors) Table I experimental column, citing its ref. [62]. The emission 2.92 eV (≈425 nm) matches the classic CaF2:Eu2+ blue band.

hosts.note: anomalous (impurity-trapped exciton) red emission at 600 nm, 2.2 us at 7.5 K; 245 nm band partly Ce3+ contamination
hosts.source: E. A. Radzhabov, R. Yu. Shendrik, arXiv:1511.00385 "Anomalous europium luminescence in LaF3"
Not obtained — gap (Eu2+ is rarely stabilized in NaYF4).

Inorganics 14, 115 (2026?) MDPI "Photoluminescence of X-Ray-Generated Sm2+ in Co-Precipitated SrF2:Sm3+ Nanocrystals" (automated extraction; year per MDPI volume 14 — verify). Radzhabov, Opt. Mater. 85, 127 (2018) gives a narrow line at 697.2 nm (SrF2) / 696.8 nm (BaF2) — the same 696-697 nm line, which MDPI assigns to 5D0->7F1.
hosts.note: In cubic (Oh) SrF2 sites 5D0->7F0 is strictly forbidden; the prominent ~697 nm line is 5D0->7F1 (MD). The full 7F_J manifold in SrF2/CaF2 (Wood & Kaiser, Phys. Rev. 126, 2079 (1962); Axe & Sorokin, Phys. Rev. 130, 945 (1963)) was not retrieved — gap; free-ion 7F_J from NIST given above are a close proxy (host shifts are tens of cm-1).
5d->4f broadband dominates (4f55d below 5D0 in CaF2); weak lines 703.5, 691.5 nm
hosts.source: E. A. Radzhabov, Opt. Mater. 85, 127 (2018), "Spectroscopy of divalent samarium in alkaline-earth fluorides" (automated extraction)
E. Radzhabov, R. Shendrik, V. Pankratov, J. Lumin. 252, 119271 (2022) "Emission of Tm2+ in alkaline-earth fluoride crystals" (automated extraction; "near 1120 / 1180 nm").
quoted in Radzhabov & Shendrik arXiv:1511.00385 citing Moine et al. (1989)

gaps: Sm2+ 7F_J / 5D1 / 5D2 crystal-field levels in SrF2, CaF2, BaFCl (primary: Wood & Kaiser 1962; Axe & Sorokin 1963; BaFCl hole-burning papers) not retrieved.
Ce3+ 5d1..5 band positions in LaF3 and beta-NaYF4 from Dorenbos compilations not verified.
